synopsis: RoadRunner, Scene Builder and Scenario create and reconstruct 3D environments from GIS, maps, point clouds and recorded data, and export to CARLA, dSPACE ASM and IPG CarMaker; however, the base editor remains road-oriented and work-site semantics require custom assets and data structures [f8605, f8606, f8607]. Cross-chapter precedents include on-road UAV orthomosaic imports demonstrated in 2021 and academic South African mining collision-avoidance simulations investigating steering-rate-based collision prediction, not operational validation [f3798, f1729]. The MathWorks stack has shipped off-road examples in R2026b, including an autonomous excavator, backhoe truck loading and an open-pit haul truck, but component integration still requires calibration of material, actor, dynamics and timing semantics [f15878, f8729]. RoadRunner with Automated Driving Toolbox reconstructs and replays camera, lidar, GPS and IMU logs, with fidelity bounded by tracking and map-reconstruction accuracy [f8656, f8657]. Licensing is commercial, annual or perpetual per product, and current pricing requires a quote; an unofficial January 2024 list gives RoadRunner prices of 4,680 annually and 9,360 perpetually, presumed USD and indicative only, while academic licenses do not allow concurrent use [f8958, f9155, f16144, f8905]. RoadRunner itself does not require MATLAB or Simulink, although the proposed middle-cost engineering stack combines them with RoadRunner and other simulation tools [f8385, f9285].
